question: Should OpenClaw enforce plugin private-import boundaries with a redesigned runtime/AST-backed policy before this PR merges, or intentionally ship this static fail-closed loader policy with known compatibility and bypass risks?
rationale: The change defines a plugin security and compatibility boundary; the submitted implementation has concrete bypasses and can break existing plugin loads, so maintainer intent is required for the enforcement model and rollout plan.

options.title: Redesign Before Merge
options.body: Rework the PR around runtime/module-resolution enforcement or AST-backed static analysis with dependency traversal, then add compatibility proof for real plugins before landing.

options.title: Stage As Diagnostic First
options.body: Convert the policy into a warning or opt-in diagnostic path while collecting plugin compatibility data before any default fail-closed rollout.

options.title: Accept Static Policy Risk
options.body: Maintain the current static scanner and own the known bypass and upgrade risks as an intentional hardening step.

recommendation.title: Redesign Before Merge
recommendation.body: Rework the PR around runtime/module-resolution enforcement or AST-backed static analysis with dependency traversal, then add compatibility proof for real plugins before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent owns the submitted PR and has recent merged history in the adjacent plugin SDK loader area.
